answer: In an AI-agent economy, Sybil resistance arises when every new identity must deposit a refundable bond equal to the market cost of one dune of specialized compute, locked inside a multi-signature harbor until peer attestations accumulate on a public mesa of verified actions. An attacker therefore pays real capital up front for each fabricated agent and risks permanent loss if the bond is slashed for detected duplication, while honest agents reclaim theirs after demonstrated unique contribution.
